classification.difficultyReason: Students count intersections or recognise tangency in each sketch and directly apply the taught correspondence with the discriminant's sign.

content.prompt: What would be the value of the discriminant $\Delta=b^{2}-4ac$ from solving the following equations simultaneously? Answer with $\Delta<0$, $\Delta=0$, or $\Delta>0$.

spec.description: Unticked axes with arrowheads at both ends; an upward parabola has its vertex left of the vertical axis and above the horizontal axis. The rising line through the origin stays below the parabola. Internal drawing coordinates express qualitative geometry only and are not printed givens. The origin O label is omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: The line and parabola have no real intersection.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph remains visible; discriminant classification appears only in answers.

answer.worked: The graphs have no points of intersection, so the resulting quadratic has no real solutions. Hence $\Delta<0$.

spec.description: Unticked axes with arrowheads at both ends; a downward parabola has its maximum on the vertical axis above the horizontal axis. A rising line through the origin crosses the parabola below-left and above-right of the origin. Internal drawing coordinates are not printed givens. The origin O label is omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: The line and parabola have two distinct real intersections.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph remains visible; discriminant classification appears only in answers.

inlines.text: The graphs intersect twice, giving two distinct real solutions. Hence

spec.description: Unticked axes with arrowheads at both ends; an upward parabola has its minimum on the vertical axis below the horizontal axis. A rising line with a negative vertical intercept is tangent to the right branch below the horizontal axis. Internal drawing coordinates guarantee tangency and are not printed givens. The origin O label is omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: The line and parabola touch at exactly one point; their difference is a perfect square.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph remains visible; discriminant classification appears only in answers.

answer.worked: The line is tangent to the parabola, giving one point of intersection. The resulting quadratic has equal roots, so $\Delta=0$.
